title: Average site area of proposed lots (Table 2B)
text: C4.1.1 Development which complies with the dwelling type and site area provisions set out in Table 2B and the following provisions. Table 2B Site area requirements, Site area per dwelling (m2): R2 Min 5000; R2.5 Min 4000; R5 Min 2000; R10 Min 875, Av 1000 [struck through]; R12.5 Min 700, Av 800 [struck through]; R15 Min 580, Av 666 [struck through]; R17.5 Min 500, Av 571 [struck through]; R20 Min 350, Av 450 [struck through]; R25 Min 300, Av 350 [struck through]; R30 Min 260, Av 300; R35 Min 220, Av 260; R40 Min 180, Av 220; R50 Min 160, Av 180; R60 Min 120, Av 150; R80 Min 100, Av 120; R100-SL Min 80, Av No av applies. Proposed change: Removal of average site area for R10 - R25 coded lots within the Perth and Peel Regions. Refer to Information Sheet 5: Lot size and density. Notes: R80 site area provisions apply to all single houses located on lots coded R100, R160 and LR, MR and HR. - Indicated not applicable. Min. Minimum site area. Av. Average site area. C4.1.5 In areas coded R25 and below; for a small dwelling (in accordance with C2.9.1) that is the subject of a proposed development, the minimum and average site area of Table 2B may be reduced by up to 35 per cent. C4.1.6 In areas coded R30 to R40; for an accessible dwelling designed to gold level universal design (in accordance with C2.7.1), or a small dwelling (in accordance with C2.9.1) that is the subject of a development proposal, the minimum and average site area of Table 2B may be reduced by up to 35 per cent, provided that: i. for single houses, no site is less than 100m2; and ii. for development or subdivision of 4 or more dwellings or sites, the site area reduction is limited to a maximum 50 per cent of the total number of dwellings or sites. C4.1.7 In areas coded R50 and above; for an accessible dwelling designed to gold level universal design (in accordance with C2.7.1), or a small dwelling (in accordance with C2.9.1) that is the subject of a development proposal, the minimum and average site area of Table 2B may be reduced by up to 35 per cent, provided that: i. for single houses, no site is less than 100m2; and ii. the site area reduction is limited for small dwellings to a maximum 50 per cent of the total number of dwellings or sites.

exceptions.label: C4.1.5 small dwelling at R25 and below: minimum and average site area reduced by up to 35%
C4.1.6 gold-level accessible or small dwelling at R30 to R40: reduced by up to 35%, no site under 100 m2, at most 50% of 4 or more sites
C4.1.7 gold-level accessible or small dwelling at R50 and above: reduced by up to 35%, no site under 100 m2, small dwellings at most 50% of sites

verified.note: The R10-R25 averages (1000/800/666/571/450/350) are printed struck through in a pink box as a proposed change for Perth and Peel only; whether they are operative is unresolved. C4.1.7(ii) 'limited for small dwellings to a maximum 50 per cent of the total number of dwellings or sites' does not say how it applies to a single lot or to gold-level accessible dwellings; the C4.1.7 exception keeps verify true.

notes: Applies where the application creates lots (rule condition). The R10-R25 averages (1000/800/666/571/450/350) are shown struck through in a pink box: 'Proposed change: Removal of average site area for R10-R25 coded lots within the Perth and Peel Regions'. Flagged only; kept as operative, region all, verify true. R2-R5 and R100-SL: no average (null). C4.1.5 to C4.1.7 concessions are exceptions on this rule (not separate rules, so a concession not taken cannot fail the element): the tested area divided by 0.65 must reach the Table 2B value. Coding bands for the concessions come from helper tables table-4.1a/b/c (true/false by coding) because exceptions cannot carry a coding of their own. Supply subdivision.lot_count = 1 and subdivision.reduced_lots_count = 1 for a single existing lot; read literally, C4.1.7(ii) then caps a lone small dwelling (1 of 1 = 100% > 50%). The 100 m2 floor is tested on the smallest proposed lot.
